newsitem.title: USA: Cosby murder witness in fear for her safety.
newsitem.headline: Cosby murder witness in fear for her safety.

text.p: An attorney for the woman who witnessed the murder of Bill Cosby's son said on Saturday she feared for her safety as reports surfaced she was on the scene and fled when Ennis Cosby was accosted by the killer.

"She's very concerned for the tragedy that befelled the Cosby family and she's very nervous and upset and concerned about her own safety and health," the unidentified woman's attorney, Richard Debro, told Los Angeles TV station KNBC.
Debro could not be immediately reached for comment.
Ennis, the only son of entertainer Bill Cosby, was murdered early on Thursday as he stopped to change a flat tire alongside a California freeway.

Police investigators have been working nearly around the clock to catch the killer. However, Los Angeles Police Chief Willie Williams said on Friday police have not yet released a sketch of the killer because the witness has been so traumatized by the incident she has not yet been able to provide a detailed description.
He said the woman's fears resulted not only from having seen "some portion of the homicide," but from the enormous media attention focused on her since the murder.

According to sources quoted by the Los Angeles Times on Saturday, the woman, a 47-year-old aspiring screenwriter, told police she was on the scene when a man with a pistol accosted her and Ennis Cosby. She said she was frightened off and when she returned Cosby's body was lying by his Mercedes convertible.
Williams said police sketch artists met the woman on Thursday and on Friday and still hoped they could come up with a drawing of the killer, described only as a white man.

The woman, whose identity has been guarded by authorities, summoned police after the murder and was questioned extensively. Some television stations broadcast pictures of her standing near the crime scene wearing a short skirt and a fur coat and talking to police.

According to media reports, the woman was a friend of Ennis Cosby and he was on the way to meet her when he stopped to change a tire on a remote stretch of road in the fashionable Bel-Air neighbourhood.
Cosby reportedly called her on his cellular telephone to come to his aid and shine her car's headlights on his Mercedes convertible while he worked.
Cosby's parents and family remained in seclusion on Saturday, their whereabouts unknown after they left their Manhattan home late on Thursday.

Bill Cosby's publicist, David Brokaw, said on Friday they had no plans to fly to Los Angeles and were still "back East." There was speculation they may have gone to the Cosby home in western Massachusetts. The family has pleaded for privacy.
